fr.recommendations:
• Trim dense vegetation along the rear of the property to open a clear path for responders moving between the back of the structure and the yard.
• Cut back vegetation that is in direct contact with or immediately adjacent to the structure to allow responders to move along exterior walls without obstruction.
• Keep a rear access point unlocked and clearly identifiable from the yard side so responders can reach it without returning to the front of the property.
• Mark or number the multiple access points so responding crews can quickly communicate which entry they are using.
• Keep the walkway clear of overgrown shrubs or plantings that would slow or block responder movement to and from the structure.
• Park vehicles in the designated parking area so the driveway and access paths remain open for emergency equipment.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches on large trees so they don't hang directly over or touch the roof or walls of the structure.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open space between individual trees and between trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure's exterior walls.
• Cut back scattered shrubs across the property so they are not connected to nearby trees or the structure.
• Clear ground vegetation growing up against the base of the structure on all sides.
• Thin scattered trees so their canopies do not touch or overlap with each other near the structure.
• Mow or cut down ground vegetation beneath and around tree clusters close to the building.
• Keep the open green space areas clear of dead or dried plant material that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees up to a height that keeps them well clear of surrounding shrubs and ground vegetation.
• Separate shrub groupings from nearby tree bases by removing vegetation between them.
